newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels smash eastern camp, kill 38.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels smash eastern camp, kill 38.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas overran a remote security camp in eastern Sri Lanka killing 38 security personnel and wounding more than 37, state radio said on Wednesday.

About 500 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels took part in the pre-dawn attack on the camp at Pulukunava in Batticaloa district, about 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo, local security officials told Reuters.
"They came in at least 20 vehicles, mostly buses and tractors. They attacked the camp from two directions," a senior police officer from the area said.
It was the Tigers' biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
An opposition member of parliament from the east, Yasendra Bakmeeweva, told parliament on Wednesday about 30 security forces personnel had been killed in the attack.
A statement issued by the Defence Ministry said 13 bodies had been recovered and that 39 had been wounded in the attack.

Military officials said the camp was occupied by about 120 men, mostly police commandos and some from the army's artillery division. The rebels withdrew after bombarding the camp late into the morning, they said.
The whereabouts of several military vehicles and at least one artillery gun was not known, they said.
A military spokesman in Colombo said it was still too early to give the exact number of dead. "Reinforcements have managed to enter the camp. We will only know of our losses now," he told Reuters.
Air force helicopter gunships provided air support to the reinforcements, he said. He added casualties were expected among the rebels, but said no details were available.
The LTTE were not immediately available for comment.
The rebels carried out an identical attack on the same camp in April, killing 18 police commandos.
In another attack in July, the rebels overran a strategic army camp at northeastern Mullaitivu, killing or capturing the camp's entire garrison of more than 1,000.
Wednesday's attack was the biggest clash since September when the military pushed the Tigers out of their Kilinochchi base, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.

The Defence Ministry said 229 soldiers died in the assault on Kilinochchi and about 300 wounded. It also said almost 700 Tigers were killed and more than 700 wounded, but the LTTE said only about 90 of their fighters died.

Colombo has scored a series of victories over the Tigers, including taking the rebels' northern Jaffna stronghold, after stepping up its military campaign following the breakdown of peace talks last year.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils, most of who are Hindu, in the north and the east of this predominantly Buddhist Sinhalese nation.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the toll is much higher.
